National Assembly
Twenty-First Session
Minutes of Proceedings
Total 39
2083 Ashad
Wednesday
Meeting Number- 33
The National Assembly's meeting today commenced at 13:28 hrs under the chairmanship of the Right Honourable Chairperson, Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable members, names have been received to speak in today's National Assembly meeting (13:28 hrs).
The proceedings will begin. Honourable members, I have allocated 1 minute each for speaking during the Zero Hour. First, Honourable Member Gita Devkota.
Honourable Member Gita Devkota (Nepali Congress):- Right Honourable Chairperson,
(13:28 hrs)
The government says there is fertilizer in the warehouse, but farmers say there is none in the fields. The warehouses are green, but the fields are yellow. There is fertilizer on paper, but it has not reached the farmers' fields. Farmers who grow crops are struggling for even one sack of fertilizer. They are pleading for help. But the government... This irony of fertilizer being in the warehouse while there is a crisis in the fields must end immediately, and I strongly urge the government, through you, Mr. Chairperson, to ensure timely delivery of fertilizer to the farmers' fields. Thank you, Jai Nepal.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Chandra Bahadur KC.
Honourable Member Chandra Bahadur KC (Nepali Congress):- Right Honourable Chairperson,
(13:29 hrs)
Farmers have not received fertilizer, and the landless problem is increasing daily. Vehicles are being impounded at the gates of media offices, and even at the house of Nepali Congress President Gagan Thapa. The reason for impounding those vehicles is not clearly known yet. Along with that, Ganesh Nepali lost his life. And Ansari, a leader of the GenZ movement, has been arrested. Residents of border areas are being taxed on household consumption goods. Accidents are increasing on the Karnali Highway. Traffic fines are being excessively increased. When will the government find the time to solve these mentioned problems? The Prime Minister remains silent on border disputes, even though the soil speaks. How long will this continue? Where has the problem of meter-based lending reached, and why is it not being resolved? The solution to that problem, and along with it, the road in Gulmi, Syangja, Parbat... (Time expired.)
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Dharmendra Paswan.
Honourable Member Dharmendra Paswan (Nepali Congress):- Right Honourable Chairperson,
(13:31 hrs)
This is an incident from the 28th. We also went as a parliamentary team, but we couldn't meet the local administration, and they couldn't come. This incident specifically occurred in Chauwa Tole, Ward No. 7, Golbazar Municipality, Siraha District. Around 10 PM at night, these individuals, Pu Mandal, Raju Miyan, Raja Miyan, Sumit Yadav, Lalan Yadav, and Shivam Mandal, went to take the 14-year-old daughter of our Mandal Khatwe Mandal, who has 5 houses there, one of which belongs to Ram. These approximately 10-15 people arrived there. This incident is beyond imagination. The local people will not remain silent. Perhaps through this very house... (Time expired.)
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Meenasingh Rakhala.
Honourable Member Meenasingh Rakhala (Communist Party of Nepal, UML):- Right Honourable Chairperson,
(13:32 hrs)
There is a big difference between compulsion and malice. It is one thing for a citizen to stop their vehicle by the roadside due to an unforeseen need or compulsion. But it is another thing to deliberately block traffic for hours, using the guise of state power to create pressure. In a democracy, power is strengthened not by criticism but by accountability. Direct or indirect interference with press freedom, displays of power, and politics of revenge are unacceptable. The government should be serious about respecting the rule of law, civil rights, and press freedom. The incident should be investigated, and the guilty should be punished. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Ranjit Karna.
Honourable Member Ranjit Karna (Nepali Congress):- Right Honourable Chairperson,
(13:33 hrs)
Today is a matter of shame. Today, some social media and international bloggers have called Nepal 'Mini Thailand' and have attempted to involve women and children in organized sex trafficking, but there has been no action from the state. The state is intimidating. There have been attempts at state-sponsored intimidation by impounding vehicles. Landless people and marginalized groups are intimidated. Farmers are intimidated by the state's failure to provide fertilizer. Businessmen are intimidated by the state, and I heard the Prime Minister say that this government is on the expressway. This government is not on the expressway; it is on the path of state terror, which shows no signs of stopping. A thorough investigation should be conducted. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Ram Kumari Jhankri.
Honourable Member Ram Kumari Jhankri (Communist Party of Nepal, UML):
(13:35 hrs)
Right Honourable Chairperson, I am speaking about Prime Minister Balendra Shah and his cabinet members' advisors, PAs, researchers, and TOR representatives. I strongly demand, in the name of the government, that the government provide written information to the public through this honourable house about which ministers have appointed which individuals to such positions and under what terms of service and laws these appointments have been made. This is because many individuals who are supposed to be working in the field, acting as government advisors, PAs, researchers, and TOR representatives, are creating a lot of problems and complaints that they are running the government parallelly. It is the government's responsibility to address this, and I demand that written information be provided to this honourable house about who these individuals are and under which laws and terms of service they have been appointed. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Rekha Kumari Jha.
Honourable Member Rekha Kumari Jha (Communist Party of Nepal, UML):- Right Honourable Chairperson,
(13:36 hrs)
The treatment of poor, helpless citizens in the holding centers for landless communities in the capital is extremely sad and inhumane. Landless people kept in holding centers in various locations are deprived of treatment, food, and basic facilities. Children are deprived of education. The government had promised to provide land ownership certificates within 60 days, but they have not been provided yet. A relief of Rs. 25,000 was announced on Ashad 9th, and they were forced to vacate the holding centers by Ashad 12th. In the name of relief, the landless have been further displaced. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Roshni Mechhe.
Honourable Member Roshni Mechhe (Communist Party of Nepal, UML):- Right Honourable Chairperson,
(13:37 hrs)
According to surveys by the Ministry of Home Affairs and recent drug surveys, approximately 146,821 citizens in Nepal are struggling with drug addiction. This number is increasing at a concerning rate of about 5.06% annually. This is not just technical data; it is the collective demise of the youth, who are considered the backbone of the country. However, serious policy debates and preparedness that should be happening in this esteemed house and at the leadership level regarding such a sensitive humanitarian situation are seen to be lacking today, and voices are rarely heard. When a youth is lost to addiction, not just an individual is lost, Mr. Chairperson; a family breaks apart, the hopes of parents are dashed. The immediate family is destroyed socially and economically. Society begins to lose its future. It is sad that we are still treating addiction as a subject of disgrace and neglect rather than treatment and compassion. The data is increasing, but why is the state's responsibility, accountability, and sensitivity decreasing? I want to draw the government's attention to this. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Basudev Ghimire.
Honourable Member Basudev Ghimire (Nepali Congress):- Right Honourable Chairperson, the government is hindering the meter-based lending victims from receiving justice by stopping them at Nijgadh and elsewhere. This is a condemnable act, and I condemn it. Through you, Mr. Chairperson, I urge the Government of Nepal to immediately resolve the problem of meter-based lenders. Thank you, Jai Nepal.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Samjhana Devkota.
Honourable Member Samjhana Devkota (Communist Party of Nepal, UML):- Right Honourable Chairperson,
(13:39 hrs)
In the Gorkha district, 90% of the Chaite paddy crop, planted on thousands of ropanis, has failed, leaving the district in a state of famine. Similarly, in Palungtar Municipality, over 900 ropanis of planted litchi were destroyed by over 90% due to windstorms and hailstorms. In Gandaki Rural Municipality, vegetables and cucumbers planted have been completely destroyed by windstorms and hailstorms, causing losses of over 20 lakh rupees to the farmers there. There is no price for the vegetables produced there. Yesterday, people threw eggplants; today, people have thrown tomatoes at Maitighar. The people are demanding prices. We have neither provided relief nor compensation to the people, nor have we provided fair prices, nor fertilizer, nor seeds. Therefore, the people are still suffering. I want the government to be accountable for the farmers' suffering. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Sunil Bahadur Thapa.
Honourable Member Sunil Bahadur Thapa (Nepali Congress):- Right Honourable Chairperson,
(13:40 hrs)
I want to inform you that in Koshi Province, despite good weather, only 31.4% of paddy transplantation has been completed due to a shortage of fertilizer. Furthermore, if there is a complete food security crisis next year, I believe the Minister of Agriculture should take full responsibility for it. Also, the psychological torture inflicted by impounding vehicles at the media houses against our party's chairman and president two days ago, I strongly condemn it and urge the Government of Nepal to bring those responsible to justice as soon as possible. It is not enough to just issue a warning. Therefore, I request, Mr. Speaker... (Time expired.)
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Somnath Poudel.
Honourable Member Somnath Poudel (Communist Party of Nepal, UML):- Right Honourable Chairperson,
(13:41 hrs)
The Honourable Minister of Health stated on Ashad 23rd that the salary of female health volunteers has been increased by 50%. I want to ask the government: how much monthly salary do female health volunteers receive? The announcement by the Finance Minister in the budget speech that the travel allowance of Rs. 1000, which they have been receiving, has been increased by 50%. Is this the same arrangement that has been announced as an increase, or is it called salary, or has some other arrangement been made? I request the government to clarify this. In the last 35 years, due to the contribution of health services and female volunteers, maternal mortality and child mortality rates have significantly improved. Female health volunteers, who constitute 49% of the government's health workforce, are working with bare feet, empty stomachs, and blisters. I salute them and greet them. I request the government to arrange a minimum allowance that covers travel, accommodation, and meal expenses. Thank you, greetings.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Kham Bahadur Khalti.

(1:42 PM) Honorable Mr. Khamm Bahadur Khatri (Nepali Congress):- Respected Chairperson,
(1:42 PM) Nowadays, there's talk of this car-related terrorism. Cars were parked in front of media houses, and at the homes of some top leaders. Who is involved in this? An atmosphere of fear has been created among independent power centers and the general public. The state has a responsibility to investigate this impartially and ensure the safety of people's lives and property. Vehicles involved have been released. This should not be released without investigating the reasons behind such incidents. Simultaneously, shops have been set up on the sidewalks again, and there are reports that this is being done by the government. In this regard, if the respected Chairperson notes this, and if this government intends to facilitate such actions, it is wrong for them to be in power and engage in such activities. I am bringing this to your attention to raise awareness, respected sir... (Time expired.)
Respected Chairperson:- Honorable members, the procedure for speaking during Zero Hour concludes here.
(1:43 PM) Honorable members, names have been submitted on a party basis for speaking during Special Time. Now I will provide time to the honorable member to speak. First, Honorable Member Kamala Pant, time is 15 minutes. Following this, Honorable Member Jhakka Prasad Subedi.
Honorable Mr. Kamala Pant (Nepali Congress):- Respected Chairperson, I was coming in and saw some employees in uniform outside in the courtyard as I entered Singha Durbar Gate. I don't know why these employees came out or what's happening. The government must know this. I expect the respected Chairperson to provide information on this.
Respected Chairperson, our party president, Nepali Congress President Gagan Thapa's home, near his home, and at the gates of media houses, some individuals parked cars. We don't know who they were. But we heard that cars were parked there. What could that be? It's a suspicious matter. It's not as if someone fell from the sky and sat there. Also, we heard that the individuals who parked cars at our party president Gagan Thapa's house left in government-plated vehicles. I want to know the truth of that.
Mr. Chairperson, I also want to thank the government. I welcome the government's decision to implement the National Integrity Policy, 2083. After a long practice and discussion, the Development, Economic Affairs, and Good Governance Committee prepared a report, and the Prime Minister himself responded to it here, and it was discussed in the assembly. The main intention of the integrity policy approved by the Council of Ministers was, Mr. Chairperson, to control corruption. We are sensitive about corruption. A narrative has been created that old parties committed corruption, what did they do. We went through a long process to establish that corruption is not good for the country, and good governance and integrity are needed in the country, and it was intended to control corruption.
Also, to reduce moral degradation. Mr. Chairperson, I repeat, to reduce moral degradation and establish good governance. For this, the government made a decision after a long process. It covers a wide scope. It should work not only in the government sector but also in the civic, legislative, financial, and diplomatic sectors to establish good governance in the country. We made this effort for that. The government recognized this, and for this, I express my heartfelt thanks.
Nepal is currently in the middle of the active monsoon. We are at high risk of three things: floods, landslides, and inundation. We are at risk of floods, landslides, and inundation. This year, an estimated 226,000 citizens from 5,000 households are expected to be affected. But unfortunately, Mr. Chairperson, the institution that does the main work related to disasters, the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, has not appointed an executive chief. Is it because there are no people, or is it not being prioritized? Appointments have been made everywhere. Even the Chief Justice was appointed by amending the Constitutional Council, challenging the constitution itself, but at such a risky time, an appointment has not been made. Insecurity has increased on the highways. But why do we hear the relevant government bodies daily mentioning specific districts in the hilly parts of Gandaki Province, Bagmati Province, etc.? But they don't specify the exact location. There is technology for this, but it's not used. They don't provide advance warnings about which district's area or which highway is at risk. The UN has selected Nepal under the 'Early Warning for All' initiative. The UN has selected Nepal, recognizing the risks. Nepal has also prepared a strategic plan for this, but the government has not yet approved it. Why the negligence? Why is this not being approved? All UN matters are approved in haste, so why is this not being approved by the government?
The government has brought forward a proposal to ratify the ILO Convention 81 on labor inspection and ILO Protocol 29 on forced labor. I want to express my heartfelt thanks to the government for this. It has come to our notice that this will happen, and it should happen. Thank you, it is my duty, and I also express my heartfelt gratitude. But the most essential and core of all this is ILO Convention 87. But it has been ignored. I demand that this be moved forward and ratified. Within that, there are talks of abolishing trade unions. That's why I feel this convention has been ignored. No Nepali leaves their family to go abroad without compulsion; we all know this. Especially for workers going to the Gulf countries, their plight is dire. Instead of arranging for them to be sent free of charge, we have received information that the government is looking to increase the service fee of Rs. 10,000 that is currently being charged. The government should work towards reducing it, not increasing it, because, as I said earlier, people are going to the Gulf out of compulsion.
The government's actions from the beginning do not look good. Mr. Chairperson, I went to Palpa once, and I hadn't paid attention then. While going to Palpa, when boarding a bus, I saw at the bus park: 'Slowly, you will surely reach; why hurry?' The government seems to be in a similar situation. It was prepared in 100 days, it created its own arbitrary laws, and in the process of implementing them, it brought leaders to their homes in a raid-like manner. We heard about raids, but they brought leaders in a raid-like manner, took them to jail, and unnecessarily... If they had been brought after proper selection and then imprisoned, it would have been understandable, but why were they brought without any selection? They acted in a raid-like manner. Therefore, as I said yesterday, you have 4 years. Walk slowly in 4 years. You have a very strong majority. Let this majority work; go slowly, govern, and do not trouble the citizens. I said this before, and I want to repeat it again, Mr. Chairperson.
Looking at the government's style of work, three tendencies are visible. Ruling by creating fear, governing, disrespecting everyone except themselves, taking credit, believing they are the only ones and no one else is, and being zero in cultivation and a hero in criticism. Criticizing everyone. These old parties should cultivate and increase production. Does governance happen by criticism? Rulers should be able to bring those who criticize to their senses. Criticism should not be made. You must have had long experience somewhere, perhaps in a job, you must have your own family. Governance does not run with such dictatorial tendencies. This is a democratic country. This is a system brought about by the long struggle and great sacrifice of blood and sweat by our great leaders. Much blood and sweat were shed to create this constitution. The government must listen to this. People who haven't shed a drop of sweat don't seem to care about governance, the state, or the people. The proof of this lack of care is what we have heard and seen about holding centers. What kind of care they have for the people is proven by what happens when they go to holding centers. The government must work in a results-oriented manner. It must deliver results. As I said at the beginning, there is fear everywhere. There is fear among employees. Why are those aged 35 and 45 causing fear? Why create ripples as if throwing a stone in water? Everyone understands governance, especially the old parties. How did they govern? What was it like? Where is even one person proven to be corrupt, even if brought in overnight raids? Therefore, one must learn to be patient.
Even in an agriculture-based country, there is a severe shortage of chemical fertilizers. There is agriculture, the budget has been allocated, I didn't speak on the budget, the budget has been allocated, but where is the arrangement for increasing production and marketing? Will the state treasury be filled without increasing production? Can resources be given to the people without filling the state treasury? And can we get out of the grey list? What is there to increase production? So far, there is a shortage of fertilizer. As long as the government cannot advance the farmers, it is difficult for the country's economy to move forward. It is difficult for farmers to advance until then. Firstly, there is a lack of irrigation; we have to depend on the monsoon. We have to look at the sky for water during the monsoon. Even then, they cannot cultivate due to irrigation issues. Now, human-caused issues – the monsoon is a natural phenomenon, that's another matter. But human-caused issues – we can bring fertilizer and give it to the farmers. Can't we even do that? The government should be able to do what it claims it will do. The government, which always criticizes others, should be able to do it. What do farmers need when they are about to cultivate? Irrigation facilities should be provided as much as possible, canals should be arranged, and if large-scale irrigation is not possible, small canals should be arranged. These things must be practical, realistic. This is not governance of Nepal like that of America or Britain. The Nepali people are sensitive. Is there anywhere in the world where people live as landless squatters, dancing to the government's tune? They are kept in holding centers, and even there, they are flooded. Then they are moved to another place. What will be the future of their children? Won't they even think about that? Governance doesn't work like this.
As soon as the season arrives, they rush to the fields, but there is no arrangement for fertilizer. Mr. Chairperson, in the last few weeks, prices have increased exorbitantly. People's kitchens are not burning. It's as if the government is saying, 'The kitchen might burn, but people have to eat.' What is the government's current program to control inflation? The government must provide a program. It must inform us; we are people's representatives. Everything cannot be said outside, or through the media. It must be said in the parliament. Production is not getting its due price.
The situation is such that vegetables and fruits... Firstly, there is no production, and production is not getting its price. Due to lack of production, as honorable members just mentioned, it is now being dumped on the streets, and consumers are facing exorbitant prices. All this is reflected on the farmers and consumers.

What is the market monitoring, Mr. Speaker? Market monitoring needs to be done, and it needs to be done thoroughly, not with fanfare. Not by giving it to the media, not by announcing on social media that we are coming to monitor the market. We need to go and monitor. Why are dairy farmers not getting paid? I am surprised. We consumers are consuming the milk, paying the price for the farmers' milk right there and then. But the farmers are not getting the price for their milk. Where has it disappeared? The government that came to power needs to find out. Is that how governance works? To bring about such good governance? Therefore, Mr. Speaker, what I want to put forward in the end is that the public is anxious everywhere. What kind of farming is this, what kind of character is this, to govern by making the public anxious? Where has it been imported from? It wasn't in Nepal. The tradition was to govern by providing relief to the public as much as possible. But where has it been imported from? I cannot say anything. This Parliament needs answers to everything. We want answers. The Prime Minister should come and explain how much we have compromised, the Prime Minister should give an answer. Even when the Finance Minister came and gave an answer, the House accepted it. We compromised. Couldn't the government have done nothing? That's why we need answers from everyone, Mr. Speaker. Thank you.

Honorable Speaker: Honorable Member Jhakku Prasad Subedi, time 15 minutes. After this, Honorable Member Roshni Mechhe.

Honorable Mr. Jhakku Prasad Subedi (Nepali Communist Party): Honorable Mr. Speaker, on the morning of Asar 29, it became known to the world that suspicious vehicles were parked in front of the offices of Kantipur Media House, Online Khabar, Himalaya Television, and the house of the President of the Nepali Congress, obstructing entry into the offices. Is the intention to spread mental terror by parking vehicles in media offices and leaders' houses? Is the intention to create fear among journalists by leaving suspicious vehicles at the main entrance of government buildings? Is it an attempt to interfere with press freedom and freedom of expression in a democracy? Seeing the established media being subjected to psychological terror reminds me of the Panchayat era. In the 2036 referendum movement, the Panchayat's 'mandales' attacked political parties, attacked leaders, and terrorized the media that supported multiparty democracy. After the activities of the 'mandales' were exposed, a clandestine group spread terror in a similar way towards the end of the Panchayat. The late former Prime Minister Surya Bahadur Thapa had exposed this in a meeting of the National Panchayat. Padam Thakurathi was shot, who was a former National Panchayat member and an established journalist. He was shot because the underground group was exposed. Today, after about 40 years, this is being remembered. Who did this act? Today, again, established media houses are being targeted to spread terror. Where has our government gone, Mr. Speaker, I want to ask. Why are those who terrorize the media not being brought under the purview of punishment even after three days have passed? We hear that they were let go with a fine of 500 for parking in the wrong place. Even during the Panchayat, the underground group was not searched for. I strongly condemn and denounce such heinous crimes.

When the visible ruler fails, the invisible ruler intervenes. It comes to terrorize, this is called the deep state. When the group nurtured and raised by the government and foreign joint ventures fails, another one comes to take over. When the media starts opposing the government's wrongdoings and exposing them, the deep state appears. This process of obstruction is new in Nepal's history. Even during Gyanendra's reign, journalists were threatened. Even editorials were written under the supervision of officials appointed by the government. Beware, deep state, your end is not far. Just as the 'mandales' and underground groups could not survive.

Mr. Speaker, the government was under a lot of stress. On one hand, the self-immolation case of Ganesh Nepali, and on the other hand, the mismanagement at the inhumane holding center for the landless. To divert attention from the landless issue and the self-immolation case, the deep state became active in Kathmandu. Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) told citizens when asking for votes, "Give us your vote, we will give you good governance." They have torn apart good governance, is this the government's good governance? On one hand, the media is labeled as '12 brothers', and on the other hand, vehicles are parked at the gates of media houses. That too, to intimidate. The media, which criticizes, is being intimidated at night because the criticism cannot be tolerated. Democracy is strengthened not by terrorizing the press, but by respecting it. Interference with the press is unacceptable to the Nepali people.

Mr. Speaker, on Asar 25, Ganesh Nepali from Mugu self-immolated in broad daylight at Tinkune, Kathmandu. Vehicles were parked on the roadside, the vehicle was locked by the metropolitan police. In extreme despair, he set himself on fire by pouring petrol. Honorable Prime Minister Balendra Shah, Ganesh Nepalis should not have to self-immolate under your rule. This is a warning of your government's failure. When Prem Prasad Acharya self-immolated some time ago, you said the state had failed. Who is responsible for Mugu's youth Ganesh Nepali, and Sarlahi's 25-year-old Vivek Mandal setting themselves on fire? Does the government have an answer to such serious incidents? Today, the youth are forced to live in despair and anger under your rule. These people who set themselves on fire are just representatives. What has your government done for the poor and laborers? Even though it's been almost four months since the government was formed, Ganesh Nepalis are still burning. Why do Ganesh Nepalis have to self-immolate in a democracy? We need an answer. You cannot say that Prem Acharayas also burned in the past. You are new, aren't you, Honorable Prime Minister? Your government doesn't have to manage traffic jams, improve road quality, or arrange parking, but it brings laws for fines and penalties? When your vehicles are stopped for two minutes, Singha Durbar burns? When Ganesh Nepalis stop their vehicles for two minutes, they have to burn themselves. The metropolitan police not only locked Ganesh Nepali's motorcycle but also locked his life's journey. They throw away the public's baskets and carts, confiscate goods from carts, overturn vehicles from cliffs, throw away 'kafal' that people brought to sell, and now it has reached the point of self-immolation due to excess. Are these the results of your government's first 100 days? Honorable Prime Minister, under your rule, if you make a minor mistake while riding a motorcycle, you have to sell two buffaloes as punishment. If you don't have buffaloes, you sell land, and if you don't have land, you set yourself on fire, game over. The Home Minister stated in the House of Representatives that the culprit in Ganesh Nepali's self-immolation is the metropolitan police, not the traffic police. Sarlahi's 24-year-old youth Vivek Mandal also died after burning himself. Whose head should this blame be placed on, government? Or should the municipality be blamed in Sarlahi too? If all areas are under metropolitan and municipal jurisdiction, where is the jurisdiction of the federal government? I want to ask this question. The bike bought by mortgaging land in Mugu, citizens are enjoying the good governance of the government. Mr. Speaker, I want to ask the government, are the landless and the poor allowed to live in Nepal? If they are allowed to live, why is the government giving them so much trouble? Hitler also put his opponents in gas chambers. The government has placed the landless, whom it dislikes, in a place prone to flooding by the Bagmati river. Hitler's opponents died writhing in the heat, while the landless disliked by the government are writhing in the cold. What is the difference in essence, Honorable Prime Minister? In the past, it was raised in Parliament and the House why the landless were being removed. This issue was raised in Parliament and on the streets. The government's answer was to protect them from the monsoon floods. And then they were placed in a flood-prone holding center? The Nepali citizens have experienced being chased away from their homes, being beaten with sticks for protesting and criticizing, having their hats removed, all in the name of good governance. Under your 'blue revolution' regime, do the landless have to live in the mud of the Bagmati? I want to ask this question.

Mr. Speaker, populists make promises to gain popularity quickly, deliver immediate results, win votes, and go into government, but do nothing in practice. A prominent leader of the RSP was saying that within 100 days, they would go to the streets of Europe, put up posters, and bring at least 100 more people to Nepal. Hasn't the government completed 100 days? When the landless living on the banks of the Bagmati were forcibly evicted from their settlements by bulldozers, people like Indra Bahadur Rai jumped into the Bagmati and lost their lives. Is the government's job only to enforce laws, or to protect citizens' lives as well? Enforce the law, but keep humanity alive. Before making a decision, consider its suggestions and impact; this is our suggestion. Finally, Honorable Prime Minister Balendra Shah, the public considered you like the moon and gave the RSP overwhelming votes across the country at your call. After becoming Prime Minister, I observed you closely, and I saw a blemish. Just as the moon has a blemish when viewed up close, just as the moon has a blemish when viewed up close and people stop looking at it, may the Nepali people not do that to you. Thank you.

Honorable Speaker: Honorable Member Roshni Mechhe, time 8 minutes. After this, Honorable Member Mahanta Thakur.

Honorable Mr. Roshni Mechhe (Nepal Communist Party, UML): Honorable Mr. Speaker, through this esteemed House today, I want to draw the government's attention to extremely sensitive and serious issues related to the government's working style, the country's financial reality, and the future of our youth. Mr. Speaker, recently, a narrative is being spread in the political market in a very superficial and populist manner, saying that nothing has happened in this country in 35 years and that the provincial structure is expensive, so let's abolish it. But is this statement based on facts? I want to ask the government. If we meticulously examine the financial statements of the Auditor General's Office for the past five fiscal years, the total administrative expenses, including salaries and allowances of officials in all seven provinces, amount to only 45.45 crore rupees, whereas the budget for the Ministry of Labor, Employment, and Social Security is 3.63 billion rupees for one year. The main source of fiscal imbalance and economic crisis is not the provincial structure. The federal government's own cumbersome administrative structure and weak fiscal discipline are making the provinces a constant scapegoat. I demand that this practice of the government be stopped immediately. Mr. Speaker, I want to present an example as a mirror for those who say nothing has happened in 34 years. The country's literacy rate, which was only about 39 percent since 2046 BS, has now increased to 76.2 percent. In 1990, the average life expectancy of Nepalis was only 44 years, but today it has reached 71 years. The progress Nepal has made in reducing child mortality and maternal mortality is exemplary worldwide. These are just one or two examples I have presented for those who say nothing has happened in 35 years.

Mr. Speaker, for how long will the current situation persist, where past historical achievements are ignored, extreme despair is spread among the public, and the country continuously declines in indicators of good governance? Teachers are currently preparing for an agitation through the Teachers' Federation. Contract employees are agitating. Did the public vote for you to sit in this chair to create terror? Did they vote for the bell symbol? Today, the public is saying, 'Remove the government.' What answer will you give? By jailing the public, by troubling the public, by creating terror? Yes, you can do these things now. My request is this. The government of Nepal, including the Prime Minister and all the ministers, you have made promises to the public, and the 100-point agenda for administrative reform by the Independent Party and the government, work according to that. We will always cooperate with you. Now I want to talk a little about Lumbini Province. Regarding the master plan that the governments of all seven provinces have made, the government must make special grants to implement these master plans. Accordingly, Lumbini Province has also demanded a budget from the government for the implementation of its master plan. The government has reduced the budget. It has given 4% less budget to the provinces and 8% less to the local bodies. How can it be implemented without that? Similarly, why are you not taking the initiative to create laws between the provincial government, the local bodies, and the federal government? I want to request through the Honorable Chairperson, are you trying to close the session again like yesterday and bring ordinances through the back door? If so, there will be a great price to pay. Understand this. The master plan for Lumbini Province includes the provision of an airport in Deukhuri, the capital of Lumbini Province. The federal government should understand this: the people living on the borders are the guardians of the border, envoys of the Government of Nepal, more than us. We have asked for a budget for a road to be built from Koilabas to Bhoko Naka and Udi Sunpoti Naka. The government has turned a deaf ear. We are true servants of the public, honest employees of the public. We are saying this. You are also servants, honest employees. Do not try to become masters. This is my request. Having said this, we want to give you an opportunity to correct yourselves and see you succeed for five years. May the public not demand your resignation, may the public not have to agitate again. With this, I seek permission to conclude my remarks in the respected assembly. Thank you. Jai Nepal. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, the order of speaking during special time ends here. (3:08 PM) Honorable members, a letter has been received from the Office of the President. I will now inform you of the contents of that letter. Subject: Regarding the authentication of bills. It is requested that one copy of each of the following bills, authenticated by the Right Honorable Ram Chandra Paudel, President of Nepal, in accordance with Article 113, Sub-section 2 of the Constitution of Nepal, be sent along with this letter. 1. Act No. 08, Bill Name: Appropriation Bill, 2083, Authentication Date: 2083-03-30. 2. Act No. 09, Bill Name: Public Debt Raising Bill, 2083, Authentication Date: 2083-03-30. 3. Act No. 10, Bill Name: Finance Bill, 2083, Authentication Date: 2083-03-30. Mahadev Panta, Secretary, dated 2083 Ashar 30. Honorable members, now I provide time to the Honorable Minister of Law, Justice, and Parliamentary Affairs, Sobita Gautam, from the Right Honorable Prime Minister Balen Shah's argument, to present the annual report of the Attorney General's Office for the fiscal year 2081/082. (3:10 PM) Honorable Minister of Law, Justice, and Parliamentary Affairs, Shri Sobita Gautam: Honorable Chairperson, with the permission of the Chairperson, I present the annual report of the Attorney General's Office for the fiscal year 2081/082 to this respected assembly. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, the next meeting of the National Assembly will be held on Friday, Shrawan 14, 2083, at 1:15 PM. This meeting is adjourned here. (Thereafter, the meeting was adjourned to be held on Friday, Shrawan 15, 2083, at 1:15 PM.) Adjournment: 3:11 PM.

sections.name: Zero Hour
sections.summary_en: Honorable member Khamm Bahadur Khatri raised concerns about car-related incidents near media houses and leaders' homes, demanding an impartial investigation. He also criticized the government for allowing street vendors and questioned the release of impounded vehicles without proper investigation. Honorable member Kamala Pant inquired about employees seen outside Singha Durbar Gate and reported suspicious car parking incidents near Nepali Congress President Gagan Thapa's residence, including the use of government vehicles by those involved.

speakers.name: Khamm Bahadur Khatri
speakers.topic: Car-related incidents, street vendors, vehicle release

speakers.name: Kamala Pant
speakers.topic: Employees outside Singha Durbar, suspicious car parking

sections.name: Special Time
sections.summary_en: Honorable member Kamala Pant praised the government's National Integrity Policy, 2083, aimed at controlling corruption and promoting good governance. She highlighted the risks of floods, landslides, and inundation due to the monsoon and criticized the delay in appointing an executive chief for the disaster management authority. She also urged the government to approve the UN's 'Early Warning for All' initiative and expedite the ratification of ILO Convention 87 on freedom of association, while supporting the ratification of Conventions 81 and Protocol 29. She expressed concern over the potential increase in service fees for migrant workers going to the Gulf countries.

speakers.name: Kamala Pant
speakers.topic: National Integrity Policy, disaster management, ILO conventions, migrant workers

sections.name: Special Time
sections.summary_en: Honorable member (unnamed) criticized the government's approach, describing it as slow and dictatorial, characterized by creating fear, disrespecting others, and focusing on criticism rather than constructive action. The speaker emphasized the need for patience and a results-oriented approach, highlighting the ongoing fear among employees and the lack of proven corruption cases despite alleged raids. The speaker also pointed out the severe shortage of chemical fertilizers, the lack of production and marketing plans for agriculture, and the resulting high prices for consumers, urging the government to prioritize farmer support and irrigation.

speakers.topic: Government's slow and dictatorial approach, fear, corruption, fertilizer shortage, agricultural production

sections.name: Special Time
sections.summary_en: The speaker continued to criticize the government's governance style, comparing it to a slow journey and warning against dictatorial tendencies in a democratic country. They stressed the importance of the constitution and the sacrifices made for it, questioning the government's commitment to the people, evidenced by the conditions in holding centers. The speaker also highlighted the severe shortage of chemical fertilizers, the lack of agricultural production and marketing strategies, and the resulting high prices for consumers. They urged the government to provide practical solutions for irrigation and support farmers, emphasizing that the country's economy depends on agricultural prosperity.

speakers.topic: Government's slow pace, dictatorial tendencies, constitutional sacrifices, holding centers, fertilizer shortage, agricultural policy

sections.name: Special Time
sections.summary_en: The speaker lamented the ongoing shortage of chemical fertilizers despite the agricultural season, the exorbitant price hikes, and the lack of government programs to control inflation. They stressed the need for the government to present its plans in parliament and inform the public. The speaker noted that production is low and prices are not reflecting the value of produce, leading to vegetables and fruits being dumped on the streets while consumers face high costs, impacting both farmers and consumers.

speakers.topic: Fertilizer shortage, inflation, government programs, agricultural production, consumer prices

sections.name: Opening
sections.summary_en: A member raises concerns about market monitoring, the non-payment of dairy farmers, and the government's approach to governance, questioning where the imported governance model comes from and demanding answers from the Prime Minister.

speakers.name: Honorable Member
speakers.topic: Market monitoring and farmer payments

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: Honorable Member Jhakku Prasad Subedi discusses suspicious vehicle parking outside media houses and the Nepali Congress president's home, linking it to past Panchayat-era tactics and demanding action against those spreading terror. He criticizes the government's inaction and the 'deep state' concept. Honorable Member Roshni Mechhe questions the narrative that nothing has been achieved in 35 years, presenting data on improved literacy and life expectancy, and criticizing the financial burden of the federal government.

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: Honorable Member Jhakku Prasad Subedi criticizes the government's handling of the Ganesh Nepali self-immolation and landless issue, accusing the 'deep state' of diverting attention. He questions the government's effectiveness and the justification for harsh penalties. He draws parallels between current actions and historical repression, urging the government to respect the press and protect citizens. He also criticizes the RSP's unfulfilled promises regarding bringing people from Europe.

speakers.name: Jhakku Prasad Subedi
speakers.topic: Self-immolation, landless issue, government failure

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: Honorable Member Roshni Mechhe addresses the government's working style, financial reality, and youth future. He refutes the claim that nothing has been achieved in 35 years, citing improvements in literacy and life expectancy, and argues that the federal government's structure, not the provinces, is the source of financial imbalance. He calls for an end to making provinces scapegoats.

speakers.topic: Critique of 35-year narrative, financial imbalance
